answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The comet multiplier is published, charged in ledge, and basalt lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4017 identities would post 1953 proofs and burn roughly 5 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
